abstract: Massively parallel cytometry (MPC) experiments allow cost-effective quantification of >200 surface proteins at single-cell resolution. The Infinity Flow protocol was developed to measure highly informative protein 'Backbone' markers on all cells in wells distributed across plates, along with well-specific exploratory protein 'Infinity' markers. Backbone markers are then used to impute the Infinity markers using machine learning methods. This protocol offers unprecedented opportunities for more comprehensive classification of cell types. However, the protocol can be improved, particularly in removal of unwanted variation. Here, we propose mapfx.norm, a novel method for removing background noise and batch effects from MPC data. It is developed as part of the MAssively Parallel Flow cytometry Xplorer R package, an end-to-end toolbox for analysing MPC data, including pre-processing and imputing missing Infinity markers in wells where those markers were not measured. Unique features of our method include performing background correction to eliminate the noise from electronic baseline restoration and fluorescence compensation prior to imputation, and removing unwanted variation at the cell level while explicitly accounting for the potential association between biology and unwanted factors. We benchmark our method against alternatives and demonstrate that our approach is better at preserving biological signals, removing unwanted variation, and imputing unmeasured Infinity markers.
